decisions.reason: As a multi-model dietary supplement line close to the firm's existing consumer-health activities, it likely meets a minimally acceptable aspiration level and a large expanding firm has enough slack to keep it.
This skin-and-hair supplement is an adjacent pharmacy product with no clear negative market signal, so management would likely continue it while it supports portfolio broadening.

The move from a mention to its own page suggests continued backing, and in a stable but innovation-oriented pharma business the firm would likely retain an established adjacent supplement unless results were clearly below aspiration.

The immune supplement is somewhat more niche and uncertain, but it still fits the Trivital line and available organizational slack makes continued experimentation more likely than immediate withdrawal.

The documented valsartan problem in a trust-sensitive generic medicine market likely pushed outcomes below aspiration and would trigger reallocation of resources away from this more problematic product.

The OTC migraine triptan is more distant and therefore riskier, but as a recent launch that fits the firm's portfolio-expansion direction it would likely be kept one more year unless early results were clearly disappointing.
